title: Congress Must Stop Arming Israel
gist: DAWN's Omar Shakir argues the Democrats' midterm 'blue tsunami' gave Congress a mandate to end all U.S. arms transfers to Israel and end the Iran war, citing polling against the war and aid; Trump has announced ending $3.8 billion in annual military aid, but Shakir notes this leaves sales, supplementals, and co-production intact and lists specific legislative levers (FY2027 appropriations, NDAA Section 219, Section 502B, war powers).

themes.theme: Midterm mandate against the Iran war and Israel aid

insights.claim: Democrats won historic majorities in both the House and Senate in the Nov. 3, 2026 midterms, setting up two confrontational years with President Trump.
insights.speaker: Omar Shakir
insights.so_what: Divided government raises odds of congressional constraints on war funding and foreign military aid.

insights.claim: About 6 in 10 U.S. voters told an AP election survey attacking Iran was wrong; a Chicago Council poll found 68 percent said the war wasn't worth its costs, 56 percent favored reducing or eliminating military aid to Israel, and 57 percent backed restrictions on aid supporting operations against Palestinians.
insights.speaker: Omar Shakir
insights.so_what: Public opinion has turned decisively against the Iran war and unconditional Israel aid, a durable political shift.
insights.quote: A Chicago Council poll found that 68 percent of Americans said the war had not been worth its costs.
insights.locator: Many voters clearly wanted their elected officials

insights.claim: Vice President J.D. Vance blamed the GOP loss on the Iran war, and Trump conceded to the Wall Street Journal that 'Iran was a piece of it.'
insights.speaker: Omar Shakir
insights.so_what: Administration acknowledging war's political cost raises probability of de-escalation pressure from within the GOP.
insights.quote: The reason we lost is the war.
insights.locator: The White House appears to have taken notice.

themes.theme: Trump's aid cut and its loopholes

insights.claim: Trump announced on Election Day that the U.S. would end its $3.8 billion in annual military aid to Israel by the end of the calendar year, a watershed in U.S. foreign policy.
insights.speaker: Omar Shakir
insights.so_what: Shifts cost of U.S.-made weapons to Israel's own budget; watch Israeli defense spending and fiscal effects.
insights.quote: the United States would end the $3.8 billion in annual military aid to the country by the end of this calendar year

insights.claim: Ending the aid package would not stop arms flows, since the current aid agreement runs through fiscal 2028, supplemental funding remains possible, and Israel can still buy U.S. weapons via government sales and commercial contracts.
insights.speaker: Omar Shakir
insights.so_what: U.S. defense-contractor sales to Israel likely persist unless Congress blocks sales and licenses directly.
insights.quote: U.S. aid to Israel won’t end with a phone call.

themes.theme: Congressional levers to halt arms to Israel

insights.claim: Shakir urges Congress to strip the $3.8 billion Israel earmark from the House-passed fiscal 2027 appropriations bill, block supplemental funding, and prohibit new sales and deliveries under existing contracts, export licenses, and stockpile arrangements.
insights.speaker: Omar Shakir
insights.so_what: Appropriations and export-license fights are the concrete events to watch for defense-export exposure to Israel.
insights.locator: The new Congress should end all U.S. arms transfers

insights.claim: Section 219 of the House-passed fiscal 2027 NDAA would expand U.S.-Israel joint weapons development, co-production, and integration of Israeli-origin technology into U.S. military systems; Shakir wants it struck, along with Rep. Don Bacon's similar H.R. 10796.
insights.speaker: Omar Shakir
insights.so_what: Fate of Section 219 matters for U.S.-Israeli defense co-production ventures and Israeli defense tech suppliers.
insights.quote: Section 219 promotes joint ventures, co-production, and integration of jointly developed or Israeli-origin technology into U.S. military systems.
insights.locator: It is critical, too, that Congress strike Section 219

insights.claim: Sen. Chris Van Hollen's Section 502B resolution, which failed 47-51 on Sept. 29, would force a State Department human-rights report within 30 days and bar security assistance, arms sales, and export licenses to Israel if the deadline is missed.
insights.speaker: Omar Shakir
insights.so_what: With a Democratic Senate, a 502B resolution could pass and legally freeze arms deliveries—a key binary event for Israel-related defense exports.
insights.quote: On Sept. 29, 47 senators, including all but one Democrat, supported a motion to advance the resolution, but 51 voted against it.

insights.claim: Van Hollen has emerged as a potential challenger to Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader, which the author says would pave the way for broader change in U.S. Israel policy.
insights.speaker: Omar Shakir
insights.so_what: Senate leadership contest is a signal for how aggressively Democrats will constrain Israel policy.
insights.locator: Van Hollen has emerged a potential challenger

themes.theme: Ending the Iran war via war powers

insights.claim: Shakir calls for a joint war powers resolution to end the Iran war, which the U.S. has waged with Israel since February, paired with a funding prohibition covering direct operations and emergency transfers to Israel.
insights.speaker: Omar Shakir
insights.so_what: Congressional defunding moves would be a de-escalation catalyst for oil and Middle East risk premia.
insights.locator: Regardless of who takes up the reins

insights.claim: After a classified October briefing, Sen. Chris Murphy described the U.S. military plan for Iran as 'insane', while the administration sends mixed messages on the war's direction.
insights.speaker: Omar Shakir
insights.so_what: Suggests escalation options remain on the table; keep tail-risk hedges on Gulf energy disruption.
insights.quote: Sen. Chris Murphy described the U.S. military plan as “insane.”
insights.locator: The Trump administration continues to send mixed

insights.claim: The Iran war has killed, maimed, and displaced thousands of civilians and damaged infrastructure and economies across the Middle East.
insights.speaker: Omar Shakir
insights.so_what: Regional economic damage persists as a drag on Gulf and Levant economies.
insights.locator: The Trump administration continues to send mixed
